metaDescription: Klacks exports hours for DATEV, Abacus AbaConnect, BMD, PAXml and more, plus CSV, JSON, XML. Orders import via XML file. With limits.
hero.title: Exports and interfaces
hero.subtitle: For accountants, payroll bureaus and IT service providers: which files Klacks produces, which it reads and where the limits are.
asOf: As of November 2026. Formats and features change with every update; the source code on GitHub is authoritative.
contentHtml:
The short version

Klacks plans staff and assignments. Klacks is not payroll accounting and does not calculate pay. After a period is closed, Klacks produces files with the hours worked, surcharges and absences that your payroll or accounting software reads in. That removes double entry.

Payroll exports: hours per employee and wage type

FormatCountryTarget software and file type
Abacus AbaConnectSwitzerlandAbacus payroll, XML (LOHN FlatPreEntry)
DATEV Lohn und GehaltGermanyMovement data, ASCII import
PAXmlSwedenPAXml 2.0, XML
Merit PalkEstoniaPay-component import, CSV
Stormware POHODA / PAMICACzechiaAttendance import, XML in a ZIP file
WinMENTORRomaniaTimesheet import, Excel
BrightPayIreland, United KingdomHourly payments import, CSV
Logo BordroTurkeyPuantaj template, Excel
Generic formatworldwidePersonnel number, date, wage type, quantity as CSV or Excel, for payroll software whose import wizard maps the columns itself

You define once which wage type corresponds to which code in your software. Surcharges are time surcharges and are shown as time, not as a money amount.

Accounting and order exports: proof of service per sealed order

FormatCountryTarget software and file type
DATEV booking batchGermanyCSV in DATEV format
BMD NTCSAustriaCSV
SIE 4BSwedenText file for accounting programs such as Fortnox or Visma eEkonomi
KROS OMEGASlovakiaJournal import, text file
PANTHEONCroatia, SloveniaBooking journal, Excel
MOVEIN.DATIsraelBooking import, fixed-length text file
Zoho BooksUnited Arab EmiratesManual journals, CSV
CSV, JSON, XMLworldwideStructured raw data for your own reports and systems

The order export is a proof of service, not an invoice. Invoicing stays with your accounting software.

How an export works

  1. The planning of the period is closed (period closing). Only closed entries are exported.
  2. An administrator switches on the formats you need. CSV, JSON and XML are always available.
  3. You choose the format and the period, and Klacks produces the file for download.

Inbound: orders from your ERP

An ERP system can drop orders as an XML file into a folder of Klacks. Klacks checks the folder regularly, creates customers and orders as drafts and keeps a ledger of every file. A planner or administrator seals the drafts by hand. The file format is a Klacks-specific XML schema.

There are no vendor-specific connectors for individual ERP products. An IT service provider produces the XML file from the ERP. Qualifications are not imported; the planner adds them when sealing.

Limits you should know

  • The formats are built from the vendors' format descriptions and sample files and protected by regression tests on the exact file content. That does not prove that your software accepts the file: an import into the respective target software is not yet confirmed for every format, and Klacks claims no certification by the vendors.
  • Run a trial import with your software before productive use. If your version differs, send us a sample file so that we can check the format.
  • Klacks does not calculate pay, does not issue wage statements and does not report to authorities or social insurance.

For IT service providers

Klacks is released under the AGPL-3.0-only and can be used without a licence fee. Service providers may install and support Klacks for their customers and charge for setup, integration and maintenance. They publish their own changes under the AGPL, for everyone who uses their installation over a network. Anyone who does not want that needs a commercial licence; details are on the licence page.

Brand names such as DATEV, Abacus, BMD, Fortnox or Visma belong to their owners and are named only to identify the target format.
